release_gates.title: Signed fill/lot/value/fees/realized-PnL ledger shared by entries, exits, GTT children and risk state
met: Immutable signed increments with average-cost replay: kite_execution_increments.
Inventory, average cost, fees and realized PnL derived in ONE BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction at synchronous=FULL: kite_inventory.
Duplicate, older-cumulative and reordered evidence converge; a crash before projection books neither quantity nor value.
Corrections and order-identity contradictions are quarantined in kite_execution_conflicts, never applied and never dropped.
Journal entries (execution_lifecycle._book_entry) and broker exits (monitor._book_exit) settle in it.
Partial exits now book their realized PnL instead of setting pnl_reconciliation_required.
state.daily_realized_pnl / _strict — the INR daily-loss breaker input — sum the ledger; the ledger read is deliberately not exception-swallowed, so it cannot fail open.
Quarantined evidence blocks automatic entries via autoexec_preflight.
Lot size is recorded on every increment from the instrument's own payload and projected onto the holding (Inventory.net_lots); quantity remains the unit for all value and risk figures.

Broker charges are fetched per order from /charges/orders and recorded against that order's fills; a cost may not be recorded without provenance, and Inventory.realized_is_gross reports whether the realized figure is still gross of costs.
Exchange timestamps from the postback drive replay ordering; a missing one records 0 rather than an arrival time posing as ordering information.

The exit path distinguishes BOOKED / ALREADY / ABSENT / UNKNOWN. Only ABSENT reaches the legacy single-price accumulator, so an unreadable ledger or evidence it already holds can no longer be double-booked into the daily-loss breaker; UNKNOWN books nowhere and blocks auto-entry.
GTT child fills now reach the ledger as source='gtt' once attributed (see P0-3).
not_met: Charges are best effort. A failed /charges/orders call leaves the holding gross of costs; nothing retries it yet.
Positions whose entry predates the ledger, and all paper positions, still book through the legacy single-price accumulator.
No process-level fencing (P0-2): concurrency is proven across threads on one SQLite database, not across engine workers.

release_gates.title: Process-level ownership/fencing across protection, registry projection and exits
release_gates.evidence: Not worked. Use a single engine writer.
met: kite_execution_leases: one holder per (scope, account, user, symbol), taken under BEGIN IMMEDIATE, so the winner is decided by the database rather than by timing.
monitor._exiting is now a claim object with the same set-like surface, so every one of _exit_position's twenty bail paths releases the cross-process claim as well as the local one.
Protection placement holds a separate lease: two processes can no longer arm two live triggers for one position.
A live exit whose ownership cannot be established is refused rather than degraded to single-process safety.
Proven with real forked processes against one SQLite file, including stale-projection fencing (journal.mark_projected is a version-guarded compare-and-swap).
not_met: A lease left by a dead process is taken over after its TTL. The durable fence against a duplicate SELL is the position's own exit_order_id, persisted before the network call; the lease closes the window in which two LIVE processes race inside one preparation, it does not replace that fence.
Paper positions take no lease by design, so multi-process simulation is not fenced.
No test kills a process mid-preparation; the restart case is exercised by expiry, not by SIGKILL.

release_gates.title: Independent recovery cadence, authenticated event capture, GTT child/order attribution and uncertain-GTT reconciliation
met: A GTT child order is attributed from the broker's own state — the armed trigger must no longer be resting AND fresh signed holdings must have shrunk by exactly this fill — rather than from a bare symbol match.
Attribution can only CLOSE a registry row; it never places an order. The failure it removes is believing we still hold something the broker already sold, and later market-selling it again.
Anything inconclusive — a resting trigger, an unanswered holdings read, a holding that did not shrink by this fill — is refused, flagged for reconciliation and blocks automatic entry.
Only documented endpoints are used. No undocumented field is sent on a protective-stop request.
not_met: No independent recovery watchdog: recovery is still invoked by scan reconciliation and postbacks.
A missed postback that never arrives is not detected by anything on a timer.
Uncertain-GTT reconciliation still requires an operator.

release_gates.title: Canonical strict persistence and portfolio risk
release_gates.evidence: Not worked. The ledger is one transactional store, but the position registry, reserved capital and drawdown state remain separate.
met: A registry that cannot be READ no longer presents itself as empty: it raises RegistryUnreadable, records the reason, refuses to overwrite the stored blob with what is in memory, and blocks automatic entry.
Scoped to the account rather than the global kill switch: one corrupt blob stops that account, not every engine.
Fees and realized values share the ledger's transactional account state.
not_met: Drawdown, aggregate open risk and exposure limits still read separate stores rather than one transactional account state.
Reserved capital is not reconciled against fresh broker balances.

release_gates.title: Real executable-contract dataset and chronological validation
release_gates.evidence:
Both untested dimensions were closed on 2026-09-07: the SHORT side and the INTRADAY timeframes. Eight cells in total, and every one fails with NEGATIVE GROSS PnL before a single rupee of cost.
Daily continuous (2018-2026, 341 symbols): long 3,200 trades gross -7,134; short 2,621 trades gross -41,121 — the short side is 5.8x WORSE, not the missing half.
Intraday per-contract minute (428 symbols, ~3 months): long@5min 26,606 trades gross -42,390; short@5min 26,533 gross -43,353; long@15min 9,354 gross -16,298; short@15min 9,644 gross -22,198; long@60min 2,127 gross -2,964; short@60min 2,569 gross -18,000. Holdouts negative throughout; short@5min had ZERO profitable symbols out of 427.
About 77,000 trades across 8 cells, 2 sides, 4 timeframes and ~430 instruments. No cell passed.
blocked_by: Options remain unmeasurable, by probe not inference: an expired future returns "invalid token" (HTTP 400) with its token in hand, and an expired option returns zero candles.
The intraday series is one contract's life, about three months, so its holdout is weeks. Those cells are a hint rather than a measurement — but they point the same way as the deep daily ones.
Long and short were measured separately; running both together, and the margin that would consume, is not modelled. Nothing suggests the combination rescues two negative halves.

release_gates.title: Versioned calendar/instrument evidence and candle finality
Unified readiness API/UI and operational runbook
release_gates.evidence: autoexec_preflight gained a ledger reason; there is still no unified readiness API, no alerting and no tested rollback.

test_limitations: Protocol fixtures are not market-performance evidence.
Cross-process tests fork against one SQLite file; they do not cover two hosts or a network filesystem.
No process is killed mid-preparation; the restart case is exercised through lease expiry.
The crash test injects a failure inside the ledger transaction; it is not a process kill.
No live broker, no live order and no real fill was involved in any check here.
The /charges/orders and GTT response shapes are exercised through fixtures, not against Zerodha.

review_methods: targeted source reads of the execution modules
graph.limitation: The graph answered orientation only; the execution-path reasoning came from reading the modules.
